terms.definition: A single-celled living organism with a true nucleus, larger and more active than a bacterium.
terms.function: A complete living organism in one cell that can move and eat.
terms.whereItIs: In ponds, oceans, soil, and inside other living things.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the simplest 'animal-like' cell in the microbial world.

terms.definition: A long whip-like tail that some protozoa use to swim.
terms.function: Whips back and forth to move the cell through water.
terms.whereItIs: A tail-like structure extending from some protozoa.
terms.whyItMatters: It is one way a protozoan can travel and hunt.

terms.definition: A temporary 'false foot' that an amoeba stretches out to move and capture food.
terms.function: Lets the amoeba slide forward and pull in food.
terms.whereItIs: Formed at the edge of an amoeba as it flows.
terms.whyItMatters: It is how an amoeba is able to move and feed.

terms.definition: The small sac inside a protozoan that holds the food it has captured.
terms.function: Holds and digests the food the cell swallowed.
terms.whereItIs: Inside the cell body of the protozoan.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the way a single-celled protozoan digests what it is eaten.

terms.definition: The true nucleus that holds the genetic material of a protozoan.
terms.whereItIs: Inside the cell in the center.
terms.whyItMatters: The true nucleus is what separates a protozoan from a bacterium.
